children: Brazil's central bank announced on Friday a series of measures to strengthen the disclosure of financial institutions in offering and granting credit, in a move that comes amid growing concern among policymakers over household debt levels in the country.
The measures aim to provide consumers with more protection and information about credit offers, while reducing cases that may contribute to excessive indebtedness, it said in a statement.
The central bank will require banks to provide clients with mechanisms to block advertising and proactive credit offers
For financially vulnerable customers, "credit offers will require prior, specific and explicit authorization, and may only be aimed at improving their financial conditions," it said
Banks will have to provide customers with information on their existing credit operations, as well as simulations of the costs of new loans and alerts for higher-risk situations
The central bank also announced stricter rules governing credit offers during the initiation of transactions with the instant payment system Pix
The new measures will be effective between March and early July 2027
Reuters reported this week, citing sources, that the central bank was preparing a package of measures to curb rising household indebtedness, including stricter disclosure requirements for lenders
